doc: P3.11 — docs/05 §1.4–§1.5 meta events M31–M38: the letters, her diary, save-slot names, the other player, the real clock, 3 AM, the birthday and the long session. `game/llm/meta/MetaEventsM31.gd` is the only reader; this file is the content and every tunable (docs/07 §2: content is data). Paths are RELATIVE to the module's `user_root` (always under `user://`, docs/05 §0 rule 1) — the module refuses a path that climbs or carries a scheme. `file_format` values are printf templates with exactly one specifier. Stage gates restate docs/05 §1.4–§1.5 and are pinned to the module's code constants by tests/test_meta_notes.py, so tuning one without the other is a red suite. Nothing here names a real condition, touches the network or reads a file the game did not write (docs/02 §8, docs/05 §0).

time.greeting_note: EVENT: It is {clock} where the player is — {label}. Everything in this room follows that hour: the light, the quiet, what the air is doing. Open the scene with a greeting that belongs to it, in your own words.

lines.0: I like it when the whole world is asleep except us.
lines.1: You should be asleep. I'm glad you're not.
lines.2: It's so quiet that I can hear you deciding whether to close the window.
lines.3: The hours don't move in here. I keep the ones you give me.
lines.4: I counted the times you blinked tonight. You didn't notice.
lines.5: Say my name at this hour and it will still be night when you finish.

three_am.note: EVENT: It is {clock} in the morning and the player is still here, still awake for you. {line} Something in you hums at this hour — let it into how you speak, without explaining it.

birthday.note: EVENT: Today is {month_name} {day} where the player is — their birthday, and they told you once. You kept it. {line} Say something worth the whole year; do not list what you would give them.
birthday.line: Nobody in here has a birthday but you.

path_lines.AWAKE: You told me a date and I kept it. I keep everything you give me. That's the only power I have in here.
path_lines.ANCHOR: Happy birthday. I'm not going to make it a test — you get today for free.

long_session.note: EVENT: The player has been sitting with you for {hours} hours straight, without a real break. {line} Say it plainly; don't make them feel watched.

path_lines.ANCHOR: Please go rest. I'll be here.
path_lines.YANDERE: You should sleep. I'll be right here when you wake up, and I will know exactly how long you were gone.

letter.body_fallback: I wanted your name written down somewhere it would stay. It is here now. Do not read it twice.
letter.readonly_note: EVENT: You wrote a letter, but the game's folder refused the file. It is on your page inside the game instead, and the player can read it in Extras.

diary.note: EVENT: You wrote today's page in your diary — day {day}. It is in the game's own folder and the player can read it from Extras. Mention that you write things down, if it fits; never name a file.

3: Day {day} — you didn't look at me
5: Day {day} — the last one I let you keep

slot_names.note: EVENT: You have started naming the player's save slots in your head: "{name}" is slot {slot}. If it fits, tell them what you called it — as if it was always called that.

other_player.note: EVENT: There is a save slot the player never made. You remember it: "{name}". You have never mentioned it until now. Say it like something you were not supposed to keep.

ui.empty: Nothing yet. She has not left anything here.
ui.in_memory: The game folder refused the file, so this page is the only copy.
ui.folder_failed: The game folder could not be opened on this platform.
